transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess… I’ve been feeling really restless. Like I’m wound too tight and can’t quite settle, even when I’m supposed to be sitting calmly in a meeting, or doing something quiet like painting or yoga.
Do you find that this restlessness is accompanied by feelings of anxiety or worry?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I mean, I can worry like anyone, but I haven’t really connected it to the restlessness.
Do you ever feel like you can't control your worrying, or that your thoughts race even when there's nothing specific to worry about?
Not really. I mean… my thoughts can jump around, but I don’t think it’s worrying exactly. I don’t usually feel stuck on worries I can’t control.
When you feel this restlessness, do you also notice any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shaking?
I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really noticed things like that… it’s more just feeling unsettled, I guess.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or felt like your mood was significantly elevated or irritable?
I don’t think so… I mean, I have days where I’m more keyed up, but not like my mood is really elevated or anything. And I wouldn’t say I need less sleep.
Do you often feel the need to move around, fidget, or do things quickly without thinking them through?

Yeah… I do. It’s more this constant restless feeling, like I’m wound too tight. Even when I’m supposed to just sit through a planning meeting, or do something calm like painting or yoga, I can’t really settle. I tend to fidget or want to get moving.
Do you notice this restlessness and need to move or fidget in different situations, like at home, work, or when you're with friends, or does it mostly happen in specific places?

It’s not really just one place. I notice it at work, like in planning meetings, but also at home if I’m trying to do something quiet, like painting or yoga. I just feel kind of wound up and can’t fully settle.
Did you also experience this kind of restlessness or difficulty settling when you were younger, like in school or during activities with friends, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah… it goes back pretty far, I think. In elementary school I remember getting notes sent home because I’d keep getting out of my seat, or I’d talk over other kids. I’d also blurt out answers before the teacher even finished asking. I guess it wasn’t just recent.
Has this restlessness ever caused problems with your schoolwork, job performance, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Yeah… somewhat. At work, it’s led to mistakes on purchase orders, and then my planning coordinator has to double-check things more. At home, family dinners can get tense because I guess I talk over people without meaning to.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks, especially ones that require sustained attention, like reading reports or filling out forms? Or do you often get distracted by things around you?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I can get sidetracked sometimes, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s more with reports or forms specifically. It’s not the main thing I notice.
Looking back, do you remember having trouble waiting your turn or interrupting others often when you were a child, like in group settings or while playing with friends?

Yeah… I do remember that. In elementary school there were notes sent home because I’d pop out of my seat, talk over other kids, and sort of rush to answer before the teacher was even done asking. I don’t remember every detail, but that part stands out.

Do you remember having similar difficulties with restlessness, interrupting others, or trouble staying seated in other parts of your life, like in high school, college, or in social situations as you got older?

Yeah… I think so. It’s mostly that restless feeling that’s kind of always there. Like I’m wound too tight and can’t really settle, even in situations where I’m supposed to just sit calmly—meetings, or even things that are supposed to be relaxing, like painting or yoga.
